findings.title: Light-theme colour changed and dark value inverted for `.topic-meta-data h5 a`
findings.description:
The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other 30% conversion in this diff produces `($primary 30%, $secondary 70%)`, e.g. `common/base/topic-post.scss:15` and `common/base/user.scss:119`.

Two regressions follow:
- **Light theme:** the bold poster link in the embedded-reply header goes from 30% to 70% lightness, which makes it much fainter and lowers contrast.
- **Dark theme:** `$secondary` at 30% is a near-background colour, so the link has low contrast there too.

It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Mobile `.custom-message-length` arguments are swapped relative to desktop
findings.description:
The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The identical selector at `desktop/modal.scss:94` was converted to `($primary 70%, $secondary 30%)`.

On mobile the flag-modal character-count hint is now noticeably darker on light themes than before, and differs from desktop on both themes. It should match desktop.

findings.title: Mobile `.topic-map h3` light-theme colour changed from 20% to 50%
findings.description:
The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new value is `($primary 50%, $secondary 50%)`. The desktop counterpart at `desktop/topic-post.scss:321` was converted to `($primary 20%, $secondary 80%)`.

The mobile heading now renders the same colour as the `h4` directly below it (line 190), flattening the h3/h4 hierarchy on both themes. It should be `($primary 20%, $secondary 80%)`.

findings.title: `.group-member-info .name` light-theme colour changed from 30% to 50% on desktop and mobile
findings.description:
The original at both `desktop/user.scss:522` and `mobile/user.scss:497` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Both are now `($primary 50%, $secondary 50%)`, identical to the sibling `.title` rule a few lines below (`desktop/user.scss:527`, `mobile/user.scss:503`).

The name was deliberately darker than the title; that distinction is lost on both themes. The equivalent `.name` rule at `common/base/user.scss:124` was converted to `($primary 30%, $secondary 70%)`. The two-file repeat looks like a copy-paste from the `.title` line.

findings.title: Same two-argument expression hand-duplicated at about 150 call sites
One unconverted occurrence left in a touched file
findings.description: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses bare `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. Six other 50% rules in the same file were converted. This is the only remaining colour declaration of this form under `app/assets/stylesheets`. Unlike its neighbours it will not adapt on dark themes.

findings.title: Comment no longer matches the default it describes
findings.description: The comment says "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)". That default (`_topic-list.scss` `td`) is now a `dark-light-choose(...)` expression, so the comment is only true for light themes.

findings.title: Hard-coded colours remain beside the newly theme-aware rules
findings.description: `a.new-user` in `embed.css.scss` is now theme-aware, but its siblings are still literal hex: `.username a` `#5c5c5c` (line 82), `span.title` `#999` (line 94), `.post-date` `#aaa` (line 43). The same applies to `.invalid .hex input { background-color: white; }` next to the converted `.description` in `admin_base.scss`. This predates the change and does not block it; dark-theme support in these files stays partial.

findings.title: `dark-light-choose` is in scope in every changed file
findings.description:
The function is defined in `common/foundation/variables.scss`. It is reachable by all three entry paths:
- `common.scss` imports it, and `desktop.scss` / `mobile.scss` import `common`.
- `admin_base.scss:2` imports it directly.
- `embed.css.scss:4` imports it directly.

So no call falls through as a literal, uncompiled CSS function.

findings.title: Remaining conversions preserve light-theme output
findings.description:
Apart from the five hunks above, every changed line in the diff keeps the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: N%)` as the first (light-theme) argument, and `!important` flags are retained in `common/base/discourse.scss:76-82` and `desktop/topic-list.scss`. Light-theme rendering is unchanged for those rules.

Most dark values are the `100-N` mirror. `admin_base.scss:385` and `admin_base.scss:726` use 50/50, which is the mirror for 50%.
